steps.title: Auditor
steps.actor: AI: a single auditor, who holds the discussion with the human
in: Vision, functional guidelines and vocabulary, plus the entries whose scope overlaps the intent's. Selected by script, index first. Never the code
out: Delta: duplicate, inconsistency with an existing flow, gap with the vision, principles or vocabulary (flagged, never blocking), hole
Proposed scope, drawn from the project vocabulary. To validate at the gate

steps.title: Challenge
steps.actor: Human F, opened by script only if the delta is not empty
in: The delta, short and in fixed form
On request: a question to the auditor about a line of the delta
out: Revised intent, back to the audit
The auditor's answer, read-only, quoting the entry concerned. It modifies no document: only a revised intent has an effect

steps.title: Designer
in: In later rounds: the human's answer, or their feedback from the gate
out: List of the parcours it shows
Hypotheses: each gap filled (a screen, a label, a rule), with a question and a default value. The designer continues with the default value
Only if a point blocks it: see the next step

steps.title: Designer's question
steps.actor: Human F, only if the designer is blocked: answers its question
in: Card: the blocking point, the options, the designer's recommendation
out: Answer, back to the designer: it resumes

steps.title: Validator
steps.actor: Persona distinct from the lead: it receives the deliverable alone, never the discussion

steps.title: Code checks
out: A single self-contained document with no external resource, under 200 KB, readable from 360 px wide, touch targets of at least 44 px, AA contrast, keyboard usable, screens and links reachable, each listed parcours has its screens, scope from the vocabulary
Elements outside the design system: the exact list of the prototype's values and components not in it, computed by comparison with its tokens

steps.title: Judge
steps.actor: AI, two fixed questions, citation required

questions.q: Is each parcours of the intent present in the parcours list?
Is a screen outside the intent?

out: Yes or no: is each parcours of the intent present? a screen outside the intent?

steps.title: Gate · Acceptance
in: The designer's hypotheses, with their default value
Elements outside the design system, element by element
Code checks and judge, all green
out: For each element outside the design system: "to integrate" (it becomes the intent of the Design system workflow) or "local exception" (recorded in the proto entry, provisional, with a catch-up)
Or back to the designer if the form or a hypothesis must be corrected, or to the intent if the substance

steps.title: Waiting for the design system
steps.actor: A script evaluates the condition at entry and at each resume request. Human F says "it's good" when the Design system workflow is finished
in: "To integrate" elements decided at the gate
Accepted design system, re-read at each check
out: Check at entry: if the list is empty, or if each element already exists in the accepted design system, the workflow continues without a pause
Otherwise, run paused: the awaited condition and the last completed step, re-read at each resume
At each "it's good" from the human: the same check. If it passes, the workflow continues

steps.title: Proto accepted
in: Gate passed, and resume validated if there was a wait
out: Proto entry: parcours, prototype link, scope, status accepted. Local exceptions are recorded there, at status provisional
Catch-up: for each local exception, an item created in the Design system workflow to confirm or integrate it, with a deadline

contract: An idea whose interface is essential.
An accepted "proto" wiki entry, which the need references.
notes: A script opens it only if the auditor's delta is not empty. Otherwise writing follows directly. The discussion is a loop between the human and the auditor, with no maximum number of rounds: at each round, the auditor receives the delta and the messages exchanged since its last round.
A need without an interface skips this workflow. A need can also be born from a proto with no written request.

The code check only establishes the list of elements outside the design system: it refuses nothing. The block comes from the waiting step: a script checks at entry that the "to integrate" elements exist in the design system, otherwise the run pauses, and the same check returns at each resume request. The proto is accepted, and thus readable by Need, only once these elements are integrated.
The designer proceeds, the human decides at the gate

Without a block, the designer continues with default values for their hypotheses, and the human corrects them at the gate, where a return to the designer is always possible. They are asked before only if a point blocks the designer. No maximum number of rounds.
The Prototype never writes into the design system
It reads its tokens, computes what falls outside, and the human decides at the gate. Only the Design system workflow modifies it.
The prototype chooses freely. The list of its choices becomes the first intent of the Design system workflow.
doc.lede: A human F prototypes an idea to make the intent observable before writing the need. Useful when the interface carries the intent.
